title: EXPANDED SHOE STORAGE
callouts: FAMILY SECTIONS: Each person has their own assigned area for shoes and gear.
EVERYDAY SHELVES: Open shelves keep daily shoes visible, accessible, and easy to grab.
SEASONAL STORAGE: Store off-season and specialty shoes in bins or higher shelves to free up space.
BOOT TRAY: Contain dirt, water, and snow with a durable tray for wet footwear.
VERTICAL CABINETS: Closed cabinets store extra pairs neatly and keep the space looking clean and calm.
objective: Expand your shoe storage system so every household member has dedicated, organized space without clutter.
quick_win: (30 SEC) Assign one clearly defined shoe space to each family member, even if you are using your existing storage.
real_world_action: Increase capacity with vertical storage, seasonal rotation, or new shelving, so shoes stay off the floor and easy to find.
game_effect: Earn a permanent passive bonus for cleaner floors and faster, calmer departures.
six_s_lesson: Continuous Improvement means expanding systems as needs grow while keeping the same clear rules and flow.
pro_tip: Keep only current-season shoes in the prime spots. Rotate the rest to longer-term storage.
maintenance: QUICK PUT-AWAY MAKES DAILY RESET EASY.
why_it_matters: As your household grows, more shoes follow. Expanded shoe storage increases capacity without sacrificing organization. The result, clean floors, faster departures, and less stress every day.
best_practices: One daily location per pair.
Separate everyday and seasonal footwear.
Label family sections when helpful.
Store kids' shoes within easy reach.
Review capacity as your family and activities change.
home_quest_challenge: ZERO SHOE PILES CHALLENGE. For the next 7 days: End each day with every pair of shoes in its assigned location. If storage reaches capacity, identify an improvement instead of allowing overflow onto the floor.
did_you_know: Expanding storage capacity works best when every additional space follows the same organizational rules as the original system.

title: VERTICAL STORAGE
callouts: UPPER CABINETS: Store seasonal or infrequently used items up high.
FLOATING SHELVES: Keep everyday essentials visible and within easy reach.
HOOK RAILS: Use wall hooks for coats, bags, hats, and keys.
TALL STORAGE: Tall shoe cabinets and cubbies increase capacity without using floor space.
LOWER LEVEL: Kid-height storage keeps their items accessible and organized.
objective: Transform unused wall space into organized storage while preserving open floor space and improving daily flow.
quick_win: (30 SEC) Move one item from the floor to the wall. Give it a home at the right height for easy use.
real_world_action: Identify unused wall space and add storage at multiple heights where it supports your arrival sequence and daily routines.
game_effect: Earn a permanent passive bonus for more storage capacity, cleaner floors, and smoother flow.
six_s_lesson: Continuous Improvement means making better use of existing space before expanding into new space.
pro_tip: Store items by frequency. Everyday at eye level. Kids below. Seasonal items up high.
maintenance: WEEKLY RESET. CHECK HEIGHTS AND ACCESS.
why_it_matters: Most entryways have more wall space than we use. Vertical storage turns that unused space into valuable capacity. The result, more storage, open floors, better accessibility, and a cleaner, safer space for everyone.
best_practices: Build upward before outward.
Keep high-use items at easy-reach height.
Assign heights by user and frequency.
Use consistent containers and labels.
Avoid overcrowding walls.
home_quest_challenge: THINK VERTICAL CHALLENGE. For the next 7 days: Move at least one category of items to vertical storage. Keep floors completely clear and notice how much easier the space feels to use.
did_you_know: Using vertical storage can increase storage capacity by 30-50% without adding any floor footprint. It also improves safety by keeping walkways open and clutter off the floor.

title: LABEL EVERYTHING
callouts: FAMILY LABELS: Name each person's space so everyone knows where things go and who owns it.
SHOE ZONE LABELS: Label shelves by person or shoe type for fast, easy cleanup every day.
MAIL CATEGORIES: Sort and label mail slots to keep important items visible and organized.
STATION LABELS: Label charging stations, key bowls, and other quick-access spots.
STORAGE LABELS: Label baskets and bins by category or season so contents are always clear.
objective: Create a consistent labeling system that makes every storage location obvious.
quick_win: (30 SEC) Label one storage area completely using a consistent style and clear wording.
real_world_action: Walk through your entryway and label every permanent storage location so anyone in your home understands the system.
game_effect: Earn a permanent passive bonus for consistency, faster cleanup, and family participation.
six_s_lesson: Continuous Improvement includes making standards visible. Labels communicate expectations and reduce variation in your system.
pro_tip: Use one font, size, and color throughout. Consistent labels reinforce the system and look clean and intentional.
why_it_matters: Labels turn an organized space into a self-explaining system. Everyone, from kids to guests, knows where things belong and where to put them back. The result is faster cleanup, less clutter, and a system that stays organized every day.
best_practices: Use clear, simple words.
Keep labels in the same place and style.
Place labels where they are easy to see.
Label by category or person.
Remove labels that no longer add value.
home_quest_challenge: LABEL THE SYSTEM CHALLENGE. For the next 7 days: Add consistent labels to every permanent storage location in your entryway. Observe if family members return items correctly without reminders.
did_you_know: Visual standards reduce uncertainty. When the correct place for an item is obvious, people are more likely to follow the system and keep the space organized.

title: WEEKLY AUDIT
callouts: WEEKLY CHECKLIST: Use a simple checklist to review the key areas of your entryway system.
IDENTIFY ISSUES: Look for problems, friction, or habits that caused clutter or confusion.
FAMILY FEEDBACK: Ask family members what worked well and what could be improved.
ASSESS SYSTEM: Evaluate storage, flow, visibility, labels, and habits that support the system.
ONE IMPROVEMENT: Choose one small improvement to test before next week's audit.
objective: Review the entryway each week, identify one opportunity for improvement, and strengthen the system.
quick_win: (30 SEC) Walk through the entryway and identify one small frustration. Write down one improvement you will test next week.
real_world_action: Hold a weekly audit after your reset. Review how the system performed, choose one improvement, and implement a small change.
game_effect: Earn a permanent passive bonus for proactive problem solving and stronger long-term systems.
six_s_lesson: Continuous Improvement is built on regular reflection. Small, measurable improvements made consistently create stronger systems.
pro_tip: Limit each audit to one or two improvements. Small changes are easier to test, measure, and sustain.
why_it_matters: Small issues become big problems when we ignore them. A weekly audit helps you catch problems early, understand what causes clutter, and make small improvements that keep the entryway working better for your family every day.
best_practices: Audit after your weekly reset.
Focus on patterns, not one-time events.
Keep notes of issues and ideas.
Test one improvement at a time.
Celebrate improvements that make life easier.
home_quest_challenge: ONE BETTER EVERY WEEK CHALLENGE. For the next 7 days: Complete one Weekly Audit. Make one small improvement to the entryway. Observe if next week is easier and smoother.
did_you_know: Systems that are regularly reviewed and improved perform better over time because small changes prevent bigger problems and keep the system relevant to your needs.
